name: beethoven-qa
summary: How code for the Beethoven engine is written and proven before it may run: the contract decorators, the CrossHair/Z3 gate, the code standards, the boundary check of the interface standard, the pinned copy and the repository kit, and the Claude Code plugin.

exports.summary: The modules a consumer may import and the names each exports (python.json): the contract decorators through their one import point, and the release's version. Everything else of the package is private; a consumer runs it through the cli export

The commands of python -m beethoven_qa a consumer runs from its pinned copy (cli.json): gate, standards, vendor, vendor-check and boundary, their options, their exit codes, and the [tool.beethoven-qa] table of pyproject.toml they read

The repository kit every consumer carries byte for byte at the same paths: the pre-push gate, the auto-merge, rulesets and standards workflows, and the cloud session's start hook. A consumer of the pinned copy takes it with vendor --kit and vendor-check compares it; the others copied it by hand and carry no record yet

The Claude Code plugin beethoven-qa (skills, the stream agent, the workflows) and the marketplace file that lists it, carried unchanged in the pinned copy so the copy is itself a directory marketplace; Claude Code reads it, no consumer imports or runs it in its own tests
How a repository takes beethoven-qa (the copy, its record, the gate's table, the lanes, the boundary check) and the code standards' groups, limits and sources
